core_business: The Public Service Commission (Te Kawa Mataaho) is the central agency responsible for leading and stewarding the New Zealand public service. Its core functions include: appointing and managing the performance of public service chief executives; setting standards for public service conduct, integrity and ethics; providing leadership on workforce strategy, diversity and inclusion; supporting inter-agency coordination and collaboration; overseeing the implementation of the Public Service Act 2020; and advising the government on public service system design and performance. As one of three central agencies (alongside DPMC and the Treasury), the Commission has a system-wide leadership role spanning all government departments.
apec_stance: As a domestic public service regulator, the Public Service Commission does not have a direct APEC engagement role. However, it supports New Zealand's APEC participation indirectly through ensuring the public service has the capability and governance frameworks needed to implement international agreements and trade-related policy commitments. The Commission's work on digital government, regulatory reform, and public sector innovation aligns with APEC's structural reform and governance agendas.
